the calcium ions play a key role in maintaining the rigidity of fibrillin-1.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calcium stabilizes the domain pair on a pico to millisecond time scale.
the calcium binding to the cbEGF pair in fibrillin-1 is essential for the rigidity of this domain pair.
the backbone dynamics of a cb-EGF pair in fibrillin-1 is stabilised by calcium binding and that the most dynamically stable regions of the domain pair are centred at the domain interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the calcium-binding EGF domain pair is a very rigid domain pair, which is consistent with the notion that the EGF domains of fibrillin-1 are likely to form a rigid rod-like structure in the extracellular matrix of the connective tissues.

calcium plays a critical role in stabilizing the rigidity of fibrillin-1 and that the most rigid regions are centred about the interface between cbEGF domains, which may be important in the assembly of fibrillin microfibrils.
calcium binding by EGF domains is a key determinant of their rigidity, which is important for their function.
